objective.text: Account for a test's outer transaction when verifying after-commit dispatch.

difficulty.rationale: Apply the test-specific transaction manager’s callback boundary rather than assuming the outer cleanup transaction suppresses all callbacks.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: Laravel 13.40’s DatabaseTransactions trait has installed its normal testing transaction manager. The application opens and commits one transaction inside the outer test transaction.

stem: An afterCommit callback is registered inside that application transaction. Must it wait until the outer test transaction commits, which normally never happens?

options.text: No; the testing manager can run it when the application transaction returns to the outer test level.
options.rationale: The test manager treats the wrapping test transaction specially and executes callbacks at that boundary. This does not prove a real production commit occurred.

options.text: Yes; the callback is permanently disabled whenever any PHPUnit assertion runs.
options.rationale: Assertions do not globally disable after-commit callbacks.
options.misconception: Assertions do not globally disable after-commit callbacks.

options.text: No; afterCommit callbacks execute immediately even before the inner transaction commits.
options.rationale: The callback registered inside the application transaction waits for its relevant commit boundary.
options.misconception: The callback registered inside the application transaction waits for its relevant commit boundary.

options.text: Yes; the test manager always behaves identically to the ordinary production transaction manager.
options.rationale: Laravel’s testing manager explicitly adjusts callback applicability for the outer test transaction.
options.misconception: Laravel’s testing manager explicitly adjusts callback applicability for the outer test transaction.
